html:
The Platt Amendment was a US law of 1901 setting the terms for ending the American occupation of Cuba after the Spanish-American War. Cuba was forced to write it into its constitution.

It gave the United States the right to intervene in Cuba to keep order, limited Cuba's power to make treaties and take on debt, and required it to lease naval bases. US troops did return several times.

Under it Cuba leased Guantanamo Bay to the US in 1903; the base is still there. The amendment was dropped in 1934, but resentment of US control helped fuel the Cuban Revolution of 1959, as Marti had foreseen.
sum: The Platt Amendment was a US law of 1901 setting the terms for ending the American occupation of Cuba after the Spanish-American War. Cuba was forced to write it into its constitution.
